name: R3.20 consolidated repair of R3.19 exact-SHA CI failures
objective: Repair the terminal R3.19 inventory, Rust formatting/test, and round-trip harness failures in one bounded milestone while preserving the real watcher callback path, exact request correlation, and strict cross-platform round-trip assertions.
observed_findings: The exact-SHA Rust migration inventory run rejects the active mapping-review goal SHA because it does not match goal.md.
The Ubuntu Rust CI formatter reports eight layout hunks across crates/engine/src/lib.rs, crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs, and crates/vault/src/watcher.rs.

The Windows watcher unit test receives a legitimate later OS callback as a new batch after its first batch has already been polled; the final expectation of no later event is timing-sensitive. The deterministic injected-callback test separately covers coalescing.

The macOS UI watcher regression test times out before receiving a notify callback wake. A bounded readiness sentinel could be mistaken for the target edit unless its callbacks are polled and settled separately; after the target write call begins, it must produce a distinct callback batch before the 60-second timer.

All three round-trip platforms pass the external filesystem callback, changed snapshot probe, and correlated refresh checks, then time out waiting for the unchanged-probe request ID. The main app environment omits the already-supported OPENOBSIDIAN_CI_FORCE_VAULT_WATCHER_HINT_REQUEST_FILE variable consumed by the UI.
scope: Synchronize the current goal SHA in requirements.json mapping_review, MIG-002, and state.json while preserving historical SHA records.
Apply only the eight rustfmt layout changes reported by the R3.19 Ubuntu GitHub Actions log; do not run a local formatter.

Remove only the Windows real-notify unit test's final assertion that no later event remains after its first poll; retain assertions for the received callback batch and the deterministic injected-callback test's exact same-ID/count=2 coalescing proof.

Make the real-watcher UI test establish backend readiness on the same watcher with real sentinel create/remove events, poll and settle their callbacks and refresh work, drain their wake notifications, and establish a fresh baseline. Bound the entire readiness phase by one absolute 10-second deadline from the first sentinel mutation; fail on exhaustion without retrying or extending the deadline. Record the instant immediately before initiating the target note write, then require a distinct callback batch with a new ID and enqueue timestamp at or after that write-start instant, poll it within 15 seconds and before the 60-second timer, and correlate that target batch to the changed probe and full refresh.
Pass the existing watcher-hint request-file environment setting into the main round-trip app process so the unchanged snapshot probe is request-correlated on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
Preserve all later edit, rename, manual-refresh, persistence, first-open/reopen, quiet-window, and exact request-correlation scenarios in the round-trip harness.
out_of_scope: Changing watcher production behavior, wake policy, batch lineage, request correlation, or the 60-second periodic reconciliation interval unless implementation review proves a narrowly necessary production defect and updates this plan before editing.

Increasing test or harness timeouts, using request_rescan/manual refresh/the periodic timer to establish watcher readiness, adding fixed sleeps as readiness substitutes, or weakening no-timer, unchanged-snapshot/no-refresh, event-lineage, or later round-trip assertions.
Removing CI coverage, changing compatibility claims, or introducing local executable validation.
implementation_criteria: All scoped source, harness, and active tracker changes are complete and independently reviewed together as one milestone.
The goal SHA-256 is synchronized in all active inventory/state references; historical milestone hashes remain unchanged.
The source diff contains only CI-reported formatting hunks plus the bounded watcher test and harness fixes described above.
No local test, build, formatter, linter, validator, runtime probe, benchmark, or application launch is used as acceptance evidence.
ci_acceptance: All required jobs pass on the same submitted SHA, including Rust CI on Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, and the minimum-supported Rust version.
Rust migration inventory passes the current goal fingerprint and existing requirement-count/mapping gates.
The Windows real-notify watcher test passes without asserting OS quiescence after its first poll, while the injected-callback test still proves exact stable coalescing behavior.

The UI real-watcher test settles readiness sentinel events within one absolute 10-second deadline, then proves the target edit produces a distinct callback batch enqueued at or after the target write-start instant, polls it within 15 seconds before the 60-second timer, and completes its correlated refresh with unchanged vault/app-data safety checks on all supported runners.
Linux, macOS, and Windows round-trip reports pass the strict unchanged-probe correlation and all subsequent edit, rename, persistence, reopen, and quiet-window scenarios.
Every artifact for the exact SHA is enumerated and reconciled by workflow/run/SHA, API size/digest, and payload identity under the established metadata-only preview policy.
submission_gate: Keep the whole R3.20 milestone local until implementation criteria and independent whole-milestone review are complete. Verify live origin/main still equals candidate_base_sha and the R3.19 exact-SHA CI batch is fully terminal and reconciled. Then fast-forward the reviewed milestone to origin/main exactly once. Hold main at the submitted SHA until all required jobs and artifacts are reconciled; do not push during the batch.
implementation_review_status: approved for one R3.20 push after the exact-base/no-active-CI gate
next_action: Keep origin/main at a0049c751d82540a9eca12e5323c05c673beacf9. R3.20 is terminal-failed and fully reconciled. Review and implement the bounded R3.21 Rust CI and unchanged-probe wake-up repair locally, then push once only after whole-milestone review.
